0. Getting started

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-00-start.Rmd
book-00-start.Rmd

What you will learn

Install the client, choose a practice environment, and check both package versions.

This chapter creates the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.4. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Before you start

You need R 4.1 or newer (the recorded run used R 4.6.2), internet access for installation, and either an Opal with dsOMOP 2.10.4 or the local DSLite practice server below. RStudio is a convenient editor; ordinary R also works. Download the book helpers below; you do not need a Git checkout.

Run this installation block once, before the examples. It installs every package used by the lessons, the offline server and the reproduction tools. Installation changes your library and is not executed during the book build. The two dsOMOP tags must be available on GitHub; this book’s recorded run used the matching locally tagged sources.

install.packages(c("remotes", "DSI", "DSOpal", "DSLite", "DBI", "RSQLite",
                   "resourcer", "withr", "openssl", "jsonlite", "knitr",
                   "rmarkdown", "pkgdown", "bslib", "opalr"))
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBase@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient@6.3.5", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOP@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")
remotes::install_github("isglobal-brge/dsOMOPClient@2.10.4", upgrade = "never")

The client is the package on your computer. The server runs requests near the data; DSLite lets you run it locally for practice. Pandoc is also needed to rebuild the site (RStudio includes it). The reproduction notes record the dependency versions used for this book.

Get the book helpers

The released 2.10.4 package archive does not contain tools/book/. Download book-helpers.zip from this site, leaving it zipped in your Downloads folder. In R, run this block and select that ZIP when the file chooser opens:

book_dir <- path.expand("~/book-work")
dir.create(book_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
unzip(file.choose(), exdir = book_dir)
setwd(book_dir)
stopifnot(all(file.exists(file.path("tools/book",
  c("practice.R", "fixture.R", "connection.R", "display.R", "load-practice.R")))),
  file.exists("tools/dates/va-native.R"))
getwd()

The last line prints your home directory followed by /book-work. In every new R session run setwd(path.expand("~/book-work")) before the chapter setup. The ZIP preserves tools/book/ and tools/dates/ automatically. Alternatively, save the individual practice, fixture, connection, display and loader files under book-work/tools/book/. Also create book-work/tools/dates/ and save the released capstone helper there as va-native.R; chapter 14’s solution uses it.

connection.R is the one place to select DSLite or Opal and set the Opal URL, project, profile and two resource names. Leave its defaults for local practice.

Check the client 

library(dsOMOPClient)
vapply(c("dsOMOPClient", "dsOMOP", "DSI", "DSLite", "dsBaseClient"),
       function(package) as.character(packageVersion(package)), character(1))
#> dsOMOPClient       dsOMOP          DSI       DSLite dsBaseClient 
#>     "2.10.4"     "2.10.4"      "1.8.0"      "1.5.0"      "6.3.5"
ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"

This reports the package on your computer. A correct client version alone does not prove that the server has the matching methods.

Load two public synthetic datasets

The practice server has two resources. GiBleed supports the introductory schema and vocabulary lessons. Synthea27Nj supplies hemoglobin and other numeric measurements with units. Both contain fictional patients; “numeric” means populated numeric fields, not real patient records. GiBleed has 44,053 measurement rows but no populated value_as_number, so it cannot teach lab-value reducers on its own.

The administrator loader is tools/book/load-practice.R. It downloads pinned Eunomia datasets, verifies archive checksums and loads two SQLite files. From your book-work R session, run the loader once:

system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"),
        c("tools/book/load-practice.R", "../practice-data"))
stopifnot(file.exists("../practice-data/gibleed.sqlite"),
          file.exists("../practice-data/numeric.sqlite"))

It uses the installed DBI, RSQLite, openssl and jsonlite packages. The source data are Apache-2.0 licensed; keep their license with redistributed copies. The recorded loader results are in the reproduction notes.

Note

Chapters 5, 7, 9, 10 and 12–14 also use a tiny, separately labelled questionnaire test fixture for the colleague’s exact education, cause-of-death and partial-date examples. Its 24 fictional people and invented question concepts are not GiBleed or Synthea. It is created temporarily by tools/book/fixture.R, not installed as a third practice resource. Each chapter states its dataset.

Open the practice server

To reproduce without Opal, install the matching dsOMOP package and DSLite, DBI, RSQLite, resourcer, withr, dsBase and dsBaseClient. Use book-work as your R working directory. DSLite executes real DataSHIELD methods inside R; this helper creates one server with both loaded resources and attaches GiBleed.

source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

conns holds connections, not patient rows. The other resource is named numeric. Every chapter includes its complete fresh-session setup, including assigning conns <- practice$conns. Numeric chapters select "numeric" through the same configuration. Questionnaire chapters source fixture.R and call practice <- book_fixture() before assigning conns; this is always local DSLite.

Check the server 

ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....

The reply comes from the server. Check both the installed and published versions when using Opal: publishing makes the package methods available to analysts.

Use the same two resources on Opal

Optional administrator walkthrough; requires a Docker host. Ordinary readers can continue with DSLite. These deployment commands were checked against the easy-opal source and opalr resource API. The book build tested both databases and all analyst chapters with DSLite. A live easy-opal deployment was not run for this revision: Docker was unavailable. The success lines below are acceptance criteria, not recorded Opal output.

Start the practice stack and mount the databases

On the Docker host, install Docker with Compose V2, then install easy-opal. Obtain the helper ZIP and load the two databases there exactly as above. The host layout must be ~/book-work/tools/book/ and ~/practice-data/. Run in a terminal:

uv tool install easy-opal
easy-opal instance create book
easy-opal -i book setup --stack-name book --host localhost --ssl-strategy none --http-port 8080 --yes
easy-opal -i book up
easy-opal -i book status
cd ~/book-work
bash tools/book/book-compose.sh up -d --force-recreate rock
bash tools/book/book-compose.sh exec -T rock sh -c 'test -r /data/practice/gibleed.sqlite && test -r /data/practice/numeric.sqlite'

Use pipx install easy-opal if you do not use uv. The setup prints the local Opal URL and administrator password; keep them for the next step. This local practice stack uses HTTP. For a remote deployment use your administrator’s URL. The shell helper uses the generated instance directory ~/.easy-opal/instances/book; if easy-opal instance info book shows another location, set BOOK_OPAL_INSTANCE_DIR to it.

The ZIP includes this concrete Compose overlay, tools/book/book-rock.yml:

services:
  rock:
    volumes:
      - type: bind
        source: ${BOOK_DATA_DIR}
        target: /data/practice
        read_only: true

book-compose.sh resolves the absolute host data directory and combines this overlay with easy-opal’s generated docker-compose.yml. The original Rock /srv volume is retained. Use bash tools/book/book-compose.sh up -d and bash tools/book/book-compose.sh stop to manage the mounted stack thereafter. After an easy-opal configuration change, run easy-opal -i book up, then the --force-recreate rock command above again to restore the overlay. Reapply the package installation steps after recreating Rock if its image lacks the packages.

Install in Rock and publish the DataSHIELD methods

First install the SQLite driver and GitHub installer inside Rock:

bash tools/book/book-compose.sh exec -T --user root rock Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("remotes", "RSQLite"), repos="https://cloud.r-project.org")'

In tools/book/connection.R, set book_driver <- "Opal", set opal_url to the URL printed by setup, and retain opal_project <- "practice", the two default resource names, and opal_profile <- "default". These are the same settings all public practice chapters read. In your local R environment set BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD to the generated password, BOOK_OPAL_USER to a new analyst name (for example bookreader) and BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD to its password. Run file.edit(path.expand("~/.Renviron")) and add these lines, replacing the placeholders with your values (retain quotes around passwords). This is a private local file, not a shared notebook:

BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD="<password printed by easy-opal>"
BOOK_OPAL_USER=bookreader
BOOK_OPAL_PASSWORD="<choose a password of at least eight characters>"

Save the file and restart R so those environment variables are loaded.

From an R session in book-work, run:

source("tools/book/opal-admin.R")

This downloadable administrator script logs in as administrator (or BOOK_OPAL_ADMIN_USER), installs dsBase 6.3.5 and dsOMOP 2.10.4 in the configured profile with dsadmin.install_github_package(), then calls dsadmin.publish_package() for both. Publishing registers their assign/aggregate methods and package options. It creates the named analyst if absent, grants DataSHIELD and profile use, creates the project and these resources, and grants the analyst resource view permission (the permission used for DataSHIELD). It leaves disclosure thresholds unchanged and refuses an existing resource whose URL or format differs. Existing analyst passwords are not reset.

Configured resource URL inside Rock Format
practice.gibleed omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/gibleed.sqlite omop.dbi.db
practice.numeric omop+dbi:sqlite:///data/practice/numeric.sqlite omop.dbi.db

SQLite needs no database credentials. The script declares package = "dsOMOP" on each resource so its resolver loads when assigned. It prints the installed package versions and resource definitions for checking. In the Opal browser UI, log in as the administrator using the same URL, open Administration → DataSHIELD, and verify the selected profile lists dsBase 6.3.5 and dsOMOP 2.10.4 with published methods. Resources remain database references; do not import them as downloadable patient tables.

First analyst login and checks for both resources

Keep only the analyst credentials for ordinary lessons. In a fresh R session:

setwd(path.expand("~/book-work"))
source("tools/book/check-opal.R")

The check script uses the same configuration and DSOpal login as the chapters, prints site and ds.omop.server.version(), then attaches each resource and requests its measurement schema. Both calls must return a nonempty schema before these success lines can print:

PASS: practice.gibleed connected; measurement schema returned
PASS: practice.numeric connected; measurement schema returned

Confirm installed and published server versions are 2.10.4 in the version reply. A failed login, missing driver, unpublished method, unreadable mount or wrong resource name stops the checks; do not proceed to the lessons until both pass. The script disconnects and logs out. Start the chapter’s visible setup to log in again. Chapter 2 exercises switching on the same connection.

To move to a future demo Opal, transfer the same two SQLite files to its Rock mount, run the resource provisioning with that host’s administrator, and update only connection.R. No database TLS setting or study-specific privacy setting is needed.

Recap

You can distinguish your client installation from the server installation and have a practice connection.

Try it

Ask the client and server for their versions again. Which call needs a connection?

Solution

ds.omop.client.version()
#> [1] "2.10.4"
ds.omop.server.version(conns = conns)
#>   server published running missing ready advice recipe_language
#> 1   site    2.10.4  2.10.4          TRUE           2, 2.0.0....
